title: Writing Task 1: Bar Chart
topic: Membandingkan kategori pada diagram batang dengan kosakata yang tepat
objectives: Membandingkan kategori dan proporsi pada bar chart
Menjelaskan selisih yang besar, sedang, dan kecil
Menyebut kategori yang paling dominan dalam sebuah grafik

block1.tip: Pada bar chart, sebutkan kategori terbesar dan terkecil, lalu bandingkan selisihnya dengan kata significant, substantial, atau slight.

lesson.intro: Bar chart membandingkan nilai antarkategori pada satu waktu atau antara beberapa tempat. Tugasmu adalah memilih kategori yang penting, lalu menjelaskan selisihnya dengan kata yang tepat.

sections.heading: Kategori dan proporsi
sections.bodyMd: Setiap **category** punya batang sendiri. **Proportion** menunjukkan bagian dari keseluruhan. Jika satu **segment** menguasai grafik, pakai kata **dominate** atau sebut angkanya.

sections.heading: Selisih
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **significant** atau **substantial** untuk selisih besar. Gunakan **slight** untuk selisih kecil. Jika perubahannya bertahap, pakai **gradual**.

sections.heading: Membandingkan
sections.bodyMd: Sebuah **comparison** harus jelas. Jika satu kategori **outperform** kategori lain, sebutkan selisihnya. Jangan hanya menulis bahwa keduanya berbeda.

block3.title: Cara Siswa Pergi ke Sekolah
block3.text:
The bar chart compares how students travelled to school in three cities in 2022. Each bar represents one city, and each category shows a different mode of transport: walking, cycling, buses, and private cars. The chart allows a clear comparison between the cities and makes it easy to see the proportion of students in each category at a glance.

In the first city, buses were the most popular choice. Almost half of the students travelled by bus, while cycling accounted for about one fifth. Walking was less common, and only a small share of students came by private car. This pattern reflects a city with a dense network of bus routes, which gives most families a reliable option.

The second city shows a different picture. Cycling was the dominant category, and in this city it did outperform buses by a significant margin. The difference was substantial, because the city has built many bike lanes over the last five years. Walking was also popular, and the number of private cars was lower than in the other two cities.

The third city has the highest proportion of private cars. More than a third of students were driven to school, which is a large share compared with the others. Buses carried a smaller share, and the figure for cycling was only a slight part of the total. The chart suggests that distance and road safety may explain these results, although the report does not test this directly.

Two other comparisons stand out. First, the gap between walking and cycling is small in the first city, but it is much wider in the second. Second, the change in car use over time is gradual rather than sudden, according to the earlier data in the report. The category of private cars did not change much in two years, which means the trend is slow.

Overall, the chart shows that transport choices depend strongly on local conditions. Where cycling infrastructure is strong, cycling is the main category. Where bus services are reliable, buses dominate. The segment of students who drive is largest where schools are farther from home, and this segment is the main target for future policy.
